stories.headline: US Lawmakers Demand Answers Over Poor Conditions Aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
stories.body:
Thousands of US military members have lived aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln for more than 250 days [c1]. The ship originally departed San Diego on November 21 and arrived in the Middle East in January ahead of the US-Israel conflict with Iran that began on February 28 [c11], after being redirected from the South China Sea [c5]. Lawmakers are now demanding answers from the Pentagon over reported food shortages, broken plumbing, and exhaustion aboard the vessel [c2]. Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal wrote a letter to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth detailing reported supply shortages, water contamination, and deteriorating mental health [c6]. Blumenthal gave Pentagon leadership a deadline of August 27 to respond to six questions regarding Navy fatigue and morale tracking [c13]. Arizona Senator Ruben Gallego requested that a bipartisan congressional delegation visit the ship to conduct an oversight investigation [c7].

Military news outlets reported that some sailors aboard the ship attempted to jump overboard [c3]. Annabelle Loma told the Navy Times that her husband attempted to go overboard during his deployment [c14]. CBS News reported that a sailor went overboard in early August, was rescued by helicopter, treated, and transferred off the ship [c8]. A relative of one sailor stated that he lost 29kg (65lbs) during deployment [c9]. Around 200 relatives confronted acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and senior commanders in San Diego regarding the extended deployment [c15]. A US Navy official told the BBC that combat actions disrupted traditional supply hubs in the region [c10]. The ship made a brief port call in Oman in early July, where crew members stocked up on fresh produce while restricted to a secure compound [c16]. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth called reports of poor conditions completely misrepresented [c4]. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claimed online that the US Navy has total control over the Strait of Hormuz [c17]. The aircraft carrier USS George Washington is travelling toward the Indian Ocean to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln [c12].

vocab.meaning: the movement or placing of military forces for duty
the process of making something dirty or poisonous

stories.headline: Israeli Settlers Besiege Palestinian Homes in West Bank as US Condemns Actions
stories.body:
Israeli settlers besieged three Palestinian homes in Qusra starting on Sunday, cutting off power and water supplies [c19]. One of the three besieged homes is owned by Loui Ridi, a Palestinian-American citizen who resides in Ohio [c27]. The UN Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory urged Israeli authorities to act immediately against the settlers in Qusra [c28]. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert described the siege as a concerted and meticulous attempt at ethnic cleansing [c25].

Israeli spokesman David Mencer called the settlers' siege deplorable and unacceptable [c20]. US Ambassador Mike Huckabee described the settler intimidation of Palestinian families in Qusra as a horrific act of terror [c22]. During an operation to remove Israeli settlers, Israeli forces instructed residents of approximately a dozen Palestinian households in Qusra to leave their properties [c18]. Forces ordered Palestinian families to evacuate and took up positions inside the properties [c23]. Maj Gen Avi Bluth visited Qusra on Wednesday and committed to evacuating Israeli settlers from the village [c24]. The Israel Defense Forces stated they dismantled two illegal outposts and detained one Israeli near Qusra and Jalud [c21]. Israeli civilians and soldiers have killed more than 1,100 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since 2020, resulting in one indictment [c26].

vocab.meaning: surrounded and trapped by opposing forces or hostile groups
the act of frightening or threatening someone to force action

stories.headline: Death Toll Rises Past 260 Following Major 7.4 Earthquake in Western Colombia
stories.body:
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia shortly after 7:30am local time on Monday [c32]. The epicenter of the powerful quake was located in the Choco region near San Jose del Palmar at a depth of 100 kilometers [c34]. Colombian authorities reported on Thursday that more than 150 aftershocks occurred following the main earthquake [c33].

The casualty count has grown rapidly as search teams assess damage across the impacted zones. Government figures indicate that at least 273 people were killed, at least 3,800 were injured, and 377 are listed as missing following the earthquake [c36].

Healthcare infrastructure suffered severe damage in major urban areas. Approximately 50 percent of the University Hospital of the Valle Evaristo Garcia in Cali was structurally damaged by the earthquake [c37]. City authorities in Cali declared a red alert for hospitals as public hospital capacity reached 100 percent on Monday [c38].

International aid efforts have begun, alongside diplomatic disagreements regarding rescue teams. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that Colombia will receive a $10m donation from the United Arab Emirates [c31]. Colombia also accepted 58.5 tonnes of aid from Mexico following the earthquake [c30]. However, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stated that Colombia refused entry to a Mexican military rescue team by requesting additional certification [c29].

This deadly quake follows another major regional disaster, as an earthquake double-event in Venezuela on June 24 killed more than 6,300 people in 2026 [c35].

vocab.meaning: the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts
smaller earthquakes that follow a larger earthquake

stories.headline: Poland Thwarts Russian Assassination Plot Against Ukrainian-American in Warsaw
stories.body:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that Polish authorities thwarted a Russian plot to kill a Ukrainian-American citizen in Warsaw [c39]. Authorities arrested the suspect accused of planning the assassination in Warsaw on August 7 [c40]. Polish security minister Tomasz Siemoniak confirmed that the arrest of the Russian suspect was carried out in cooperation with US services [c42].

Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that this was the first known instance of someone acting on Russian orders attempting to attack a US citizen on NATO territory [c41]. The plot follows a previous fatal attack on a critic in the country, as Russian caricaturist and Putin critic Semyon Skrepetsky was shot dead in eastern Poland in June [c43].

vocab.meaning: prevented someone from accomplishing a plan or goal
the murder of a prominent person for political or specific reasons

stories.headline: Extreme Summer Heatwave and Wildfires Cause Severe Disruption Across Europe
stories.body:
A severe summer heatwave is causing health emergencies and operational disruptions across Europe. The UK recorded a provisional temperature of 38.1C at Kew Gardens in London, making it the country's hottest day of 2026 so far [c45]. The Royal College of Nursing stated that nurses collapsed from heat exhaustion while working in UK hospitals lacking adequate air conditioning [c46]. Southern Water applied for a drought order in Britain that could restrict non-essential water usage [c47]. German public health officials estimated that 12,500 people died from heat-related causes during the summer [c50].

In Greece, a fleet of 15 boats evacuated over 250 tourists and locals from the beach at Siviri as a wildfire approached homes [c44]. In Romania, authorities shut down the second of two nuclear reactors at its only nuclear power plant due to record-low water flows on the Danube River [c49]. Economic impact estimates are rising, as Dutch bank Triodos estimated that extreme heatwaves and drought could reduce EU gross domestic product by 1 percent in 2026, or around €180 billion [c48].

vocab.meaning: arranged or existing for the present, subject to later confirmation
a state of extreme physical or mental fatigue

stories.headline: Russian President Putin Visits Iturup Island, Prompting Protests from Japan
stories.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin made his first visit to the Kuril Islands, stopping on Iturup [c51]. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned Putin's visit as absolutely unacceptable and incompatible with Japan's position on the Northern Territories [c53]. Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi strongly protested Putin's trip to Iturup and summoned Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev [c52].

Approximately 17,000 Japanese residents formerly lived on the Kuril Islands before being deported by the Soviet Union, and around 20,000 Russian citizens live there now [c55]. Russia has strengthened its military presence on the Kuril Islands by deploying Bastion coastal defence missile systems and Su-35 fighter aircraft [c54].

vocab.meaning: forced to leave a country by official order
not able to exist together in harmony or agreement

stories.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Spreads to Sixth Province Near South Sudan Border
stories.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a sixth province following a death in Bas-Uele [c56]. Government figures show the current outbreak has killed 2,128 people out of 4,566 confirmed cases [c57]. Genetic sequencing showed that the Ebola outbreak in DRC began in February, months before its official declaration on May 15 [c61].

Mercy Corps warned that confirmed Ebola cases sit 35 kilometres from the South Sudan border [c58]. The current Ebola outbreak in DRC is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, which lacks approved vaccines or treatments [c59]. Medical responses faced delays as health workers at the Nizi Treatment Center in Ituri province went on strike over unpaid salaries for three months, temporarily closing the facility [c60].

vocab.meaning: the process of analyzing genetic material to determine its structure
a specific variety or type of a virus or microorganism

stories.headline: Zambians Vote in General Election Amid High Poverty and Economic Pressures
stories.body:
Zambians are voting in a high-stakes general election dominated by ongoing economic difficulties. Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second term against the Tonse Alliance led by Brian Mundubile [c63]. The World Bank estimates that 70 percent of the population in Zambia survives on less than three dollars a day [c62].

However, macroeconomic data shows a reduction in price increases over recent years. Annual inflation in Zambia fell to 6.5%, down from 24.6% in July 2021 [c65]. The election comes following political changes after former Zambian President Edgar Lungu died in South Africa in June 2025 [c64].

vocab.meaning: a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money
a union formed for mutual benefit or shared political goals

stories.headline: India's Parliament Concludes Low-Productivity Monsoon Session Amid Protests
stories.body:
Parliament's Monsoon session ended with Lok Sabha productivity at 19% and Rajya Sabha productivity at 39% [c66]. Disruptions consistently halted proceedings in the lower house throughout the session. The Lok Sabha completed zero Question Hours during the 25-day Monsoon session due to daily disruptions [c68].

Despite the frequent halts to business, Parliament passed 12 bills during the Monsoon session, including the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill [c67]. In another key action, the Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee [c70].

The legislative session was heavily impacted by fallout from national examination controversies. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister following student protests over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak [c69].

vocab.meaning: the rate at which work or official tasks are completed
a minor change or addition designed to improve a text or law

stories.headline: Akali Dal Leader Sukhbir Singh Badal Wounded in Attack Outside Nanded Gurdwara
stories.body:
Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal suffered injuries to his arm and shoulder in a kirpan attack outside Gurdwara Mata Sahib in Nanded [c72]. Police identified the suspect who attacked Sukhbir Singh Badal as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh Teja Singh Aidal, a law graduate from Pune [c71].

This incident follows previous violent attempts targeting the political figure. Sukhbir Singh Badal previously survived an assassination attempt at the Golden Temple in Amritsar on December 4, 2024 [c73].

vocab.meaning: a person thought to be guilty of a crime or offense
physical harm or damage done to a person's body

stories.headline: Flooded Tunnel in Chamoli Kills Six Hydroelectric Project Workers
stories.body:
At least six workers died and 14 were injured when water and debris flooded an under-construction hydroelectric tunnel in Pipalkoti, Chamoli [c74]. The flooded tunnel in Chamoli is a 2km-long Tail Race Tunnel constructed by Hindustan Construction Company for THDC [c75].

The industrial accident occurred shortly after severe water surges in the region. A Bailey Bridge at Tamak Nala in Chamoli was swept away by surging water on August 10 [c76].

vocab.meaning: generating electricity using the force of moving water
scattered pieces of waste, rock, or destroyed material

stories.headline: Bar Council Reverses Ban on NALSAR Graduates Enrolment Pending Report
stories.body:
The Bar Council of India reversed its directive blocking NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch from advocate enrolment, allowing students to seek enrolment [c77]. However, the BCI gave NALSAR three days to submit an authenticated report identifying individuals who organised the campaign against Chief Justice Surya Kant [c78].

The dispute stems from student objections regarding university events. Approximately 450 out of roughly 1,400 NALSAR students supported the objection to inviting Chief Justice Surya Kant to the convocation [c79]. The campaign relates to prior court remarks, as Abhijeet Dipke founded the Cockroach Janta Party after Chief Justice Surya Kant referred to youth as cockroaches during a court hearing in May [c80].

vocab.meaning: an official instruction or order issued by an authority
a formal ceremony for granting degrees to graduating students
